messages:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT: Elevated GPU OOMs during prefill on pool-gpu-3. Containers restarting; some kernels reporting 'GPU reset' around allocation. Threshold crossed: 8 events in 6 minutes.

sam (oncall): acked, looking at logs. tagging infra and runtime.

jordan (oncall-2): standing by to take over if needed.

maria (infra): seeing node ip-10-4-88-2 with repeated docker restarts; dmesg shows: 'NVRM: Xid (0x65) at ..' and GPU reset entries. Multiple pods on that node OOMed during prefill phase.

ida (eng-runtime): likely large-context prefill requests (user-side >12k tokens) + concurrent KV build causing temporary spike in allocation before stream starts. Runtime was holding prefilling tensors longer than expected.

sam (oncall): scope: single pool (pool-gpu-3), two customers reported failures (enterprise A and enterprise B), broader traffic unaffected so far. CS ticket INC-4877 created.

cs-bot: Customer messages: "lots of 500s on long prompts, retries also fail."

alon (sre): recommend emergency mitigation: 1) add gateway soft-throttle for prefill_size>6k to route to dedicated cpu fallback 2) temporarily reduce prefill concurrency for pool-gpu-3 3) cordon/evict problematic node.

jordan (oncall-2): + add a short-lived admission reject for >16k tokens to avoid driver edge cases.

maria (infra): cordoning node ip-10-4-88-2 now and starting drain commands.

devops-bot: Cordon and drain started: kubectl cordon ip-10-4-88-2; kubectl drain ip-10-4-88-2 --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets (job 4782).

ida (eng-runtime): pushing a runtime patch to reduce KV prefill retention window and to free scratch buffers earlier. Config diff: 
```
PREFILL_KV_RETENTION=0.2  # previous 0.5
PREFILL_GRACE_FREE_MS=150  # reduce hold time
GPU_SCRATCH_PREALLOC=false
```

devops-bot: Runtime patch canary deployed to 4 pods in pool-gpu-3. Monitoring memory and allocation traces.

sam (oncall): applied gateway soft-throttle rule: max_prefill_tokens=6144 for pool-gpu-3; requests larger will receive 429 with pointer to fallback. Rule ID: gw-ppf-1789994444.

maria (infra): drained node completed, evicted pods are restarting on other nodes. Observed one pod failing with 'CUDA failed to initialize memory', evicted and rescheduled. After runtime patch canary, prefill peak mem p95 down ~45% on canary.

ida (eng-runtime): observed one GPU reset during warmup in canary logs at 1789994512 but no container restart. Investigating driver interaction; collecting coredump-like GPU logs and nvml traces.

jordan (oncall-2): @cs-bot please tell impacted customers we've throttled and routed large contexts to fallback; offering to replay jobs on non-peak lanes; no evidence of data compromise.

cs-bot: Sent update to customers in INC-4877 with mitigation steps and ETA for RCA (48 hours). Customers requested accelerated patch; noted.

alon (sre): short term: keep gateway throttle for 60m and keep pool-gpu-3 on reduced concurrency. Longer term: add admission control + prefill histograming to dashboards.

sam (oncall): monitoring 20m window. so far no new OOM restarts after rollouts. keeping page open for escalation window.

ida (eng-runtime): follow-ups logged: 1) reproduce driver reset on staging with synthetic long prefill 2) add prefill token distribution alert 3) tighten prefill lifecycle to free buffers sooner 4) ensure fallback routing is automatic when pool memory pressure >85%.

maria (infra): filing infra bug to test driver/firmware combos; possible NV driver regression when allocations spike while kernel is busy.

jordan (oncall-2): taking postmortem ownership. will assemble timeline, attach logs, and propose permanent controls (gateway admission + runtime guardrails + infra driver test).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; no new restarts in last 25m. status -> monitoring.

devops-bot: schedule: uncordon of ip-10-4-88-2 after 90m health checks pass; automatic.

sam (oncall): handing off to jordan for full RCA. thanks team. :thanks:
